stem.en: A single-celled organism relies on one cell to move, eat, and reproduce. If a mutation causes the descendants of this cell to stick together in a massive clump of 10,000 identical cells that all continue to try to move, eat, and reproduce independently, what is the most likely outcome for this large clump?

text.en: It will perform all functions 10,000 times faster than the single cell.
It will automatically divide into groups with different specialized jobs to survive.
It will struggle because identical cells repeating the same tasks cannot efficiently coordinate the needs of a massive structure.
It will easily supply the inner cells with food because there are now more cells available to do the work.

explanation.en:
**Why “It will struggle because identical cells repeating the same tasks cannot efficiently coordinate the needs of a massive structure.” is right**

Adding identical cells only increases quantity, not capability. Without organizing similar cells into groups that perform different tasks, a larger structure creates coordination and supply problems rather than solving them.

**Why the others are not**

- **“It will perform all functions 10,000 times faster than the single cell.”** — the trap for anyone who believes that if a clump can "perform all functions 10,000 times faster", then merely increasing the number of identical cells directly multiplies capabilities.
- **“It will automatically divide into groups with different specialized jobs to survive.”** — the trap for anyone who believes that cells will "automatically divide into groups" because they consciously decide to reorganize to survive.
- **“It will easily supply the inner cells with food because there are now more cells available to do the work.”** — the trap for anyone who believes that having "more cells available to do the work" automatically solves the logistical problems of a larger body size.

hints.en: If you hire 10,000 identical chefs to cook in one kitchen, does the food get cooked faster, or do they just get in each other's way?
